# Results — Study 785 (Parking-Lot)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**satellite parking-lot counts (a LABELLED PROXY) beat the earnings print for Walmart (WMT)**:
long the busy quarters, short the empty ones, entered at the print. Offline & deterministic once
cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month). Fingerprint `eb607d15a2de` (WMT + SPY, one combined panel,
adjusted/total-return daily closes).*

> ⚠️ **The parking signal is a LABELLED PROXY, not real satellite data and not a live feed.**
> Genuine orbital car-count panels are paywalled and not redistributable, so
> [`data.py`](../parking_lot/data.py) uses a hardcoded, deterministic, *stylised* quarterly
> foot-traffic index, used **ordinally only** (busier vs emptier lots year-over-year). This study
> tests the *method and the proxy*, not a live orbital feed — a positive result would still need
> the real, paid panel to bank. The result below is a clean null, so the caveat is moot in
> practice; it matters if you were tempted to read the synthetic control as a live edge.

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, `WMT` (Walmart) + `SPY` (S&P 500), one combined panel: 4,652 rows, 2008-01-02 → 2026-06-30 |
| Signal | **LABELLED PROXY** — stylised quarterly WMT foot-traffic index 2010→2025 (64 quarters), used ordinally (sign of same-quarter YoY change): **41 busy, 23 slow, 0 flat** |
| Anchors | **stylised** WMT reporting dates (~mid/late Feb, mid-May, mid-Aug, mid-Nov — public cadence, zero look-ahead), snapped to the last session on/before; **not** exact release timestamps |
| Events resolvable | all **64** of 64 parking quarters have WMT+SPY forward coverage |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the direction-signed long/short forward return (busy − slow); Welch two-sample *t*; Spearman(yoy, forward); Wilson hit-rate interval; a 40-seed × 250-draw sign-shuffle placebo; leave-one-out jackknife |
| Execution / costs | **calendar-known, zero look-ahead**: entered at the print anchor; forward = [anchor → anchor+K]; net of 2× one-way cost × NAV. Gross AND net reported |
| Price basis | **total-return** (dividends reinvested, `auto_adjust=True`) for both legs |

## Forward timing — WMT abnormal return (WMT − SPY), entered at the print anchor

| subset | cut | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| BUSY quarters | 1-week (k=5) | 41 | +0.080% | +0.137 | 21/41 = 51.2% [36.5%, 65.7%] |
| BUSY quarters | 1-month (k=21) | 41 | −0.481% | −0.564 | 18/41 = 43.9% [29.9%, 59.0%] |
| SLOW quarters | 1-week (k=5) | 23 | −0.612% | −0.643 | 11/23 = 47.8% |
| SLOW quarters | 1-month (k=21) | 23 | +0.023% | +0.014 | 8/23 = 34.8% |

Every cell is a coin-flip. "Busy" quarters do **not** drift up after the print (1-week +0.08%,
*t* = +0.14; 1-month actually *negative*), and "slow" quarters do **not** drift down (1-month
+0.02%). The proxy carries no post-print information about WMT.

## Long/short — busy minus slow (the tradable timing rule)

| cut | L/S mean | one-sample *t* | Welch busy−slow (*t*) | Spearman(yoy, fwd) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-week (k=5) | +0.271% | +0.539 | +0.692% (+0.620) | −0.024 |
| 1-month (k=21) | −0.316% | −0.391 | −0.504% (−0.266) | −0.041 |

The busy-minus-slow spread is statistically indistinguishable from zero at both horizons
(|*t*| < 0.55), it **flips sign** between the 1-week and 1-month window, and the rank correlation
between the parking YoY and the forward return is essentially **0** (−0.02, −0.04). There is no
monotone "more cars → higher forward return" relationship.

## Sign-shuffle placebo (40 seeds × 250 draws = 10,000)

| cut | tail | observed | placebo mean (sd) | p |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-week L/S | right | +0.271% | −0.005% (0.499%) | 0.295 |
| 1-month L/S | right | −0.316% | +0.002% (0.796%) | 0.651 |

Holding the forward returns fixed and randomly relabelling which quarters were "busy," the real
labels land **dead in the middle** of the luck cloud (p = 0.29 and 0.65). The parking labels add
nothing beyond a random ±1 assignment.

## Jackknife (leave-one-out) — 1-month long/short *t*

Full-sample *t* = **−0.391**; across all 64 leave-one-out draws the *t* wanders across zero,
**[−0.695, +0.204]** — no single quarter is holding up (or holding down) the signal because there
is no signal.

## Tradability — net of costs (calendar-known entry, zero look-ahead)

| window | gross | net @ 5 bps | net @ 10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-week L/S | +0.271% (*t* +0.54) | +0.243% (*t* +0.48) | +0.215% (*t* +0.43) |
| 1-month L/S | −0.316% (*t* −0.39) | −0.344% (*t* −0.43) | −0.373% (*t* −0.46) |

Nothing survives because nothing was there gross. Costs are almost irrelevant when the signal is
zero.

## Synthetic positive control (deterministic, no network)

- **Null (bump = 0), 20 seeds:** mean *t* = +0.23 (sd 1.17); |*t*| ≥ 2 in **1/20** seeds — a
  well-behaved false-positive rate at n = 64 events with a 21-day AR.
- **Planted busy/slow link +2% (seed 810):** mean L/S +2.634%, *t* = **+3.43**.
- **Planted busy/slow link +4% (seed 810):** mean L/S +4.539%, *t* = **+5.92** — a real parking →
  forward-return link is recovered monotonically. The detector works; the real tape simply has
  nothing for it to find.

## Verdict

| Axis | Stamp | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Signal — is the effect real?** | **None** | Every cut is a coin-flip: busy-quarter forward AR +0.08% / −0.48% (|*t*| < 0.6), slow-quarter +0.02% / −0.61%, long/short spread |*t*| < 0.55 that **flips sign** across horizons, Spearman(yoy, fwd) ≈ 0, sign-shuffle placebo p = 0.29 / 0.65, jackknife *t* straddling zero. The synthetic control confirms the detector *would* fire on a planted link (*t* = +3.4 at +2%), so this is a true null, not a broken test. |
| **Tradability — survives costs/scale?** | **Mirage** | Nothing to bank. There is no gross edge to erode, the sign is unstable across horizons, and — decisively — the signal is a **LABELLED PROXY**, not the real (paywalled) satellite panel, so even a hypothetical edge here would not be a live, investable feed. |

**In one sentence:** counting cars in Walmart's lots — at least via a stylised, public, ordinal
proxy entered at the print — does **not** beat the earnings print: the busy-minus-slow forward
spread is indistinguishable from a random relabelling (placebo p ≈ 0.3–0.65, Spearman ≈ 0), a
clean None/Mirage that squares with the literature's finding that any real satellite edge accrues
*early, pre-announcement, to the paying subscribers* and decays as the data diffuses.
